steps.line: Layla. Awake. Good. Didn't die on the drop. Sit up. Tell me what's on the board.
Handler. Floor one. Cold, damp, stone. Look around.

The dark gives way in pieces. Cold stone under your palm. The smell of old smoke and damp fur. A shape standing beside you — a made thing of rough stone, flat-eyed, watching like a closed door. Your name is Layla; past that, a blank wall. In your pocket, faintly warm, a stub of chalk. Your hands remember what your memory lost: how to grip, how to move, how to take a hit. Find a way through.
The chalk in your pocket. Warm. Draw a closed ring around marked stone units. Ring closes, it follows you. Mind the rules in the floor. Reach the bottom.
Siraj's stone head turns, and the lantern's light slides across the hall to the woman beside him.
Nur stops mid-breath. Her hand rises to her mouth. She is looking at a giant of dark rock and copper pipe, and she knows the way he holds his shoulders.
"Nur," he says. The word comes slowly, like a rusted hinge learning to move.
"Siraj." She says it as if it were the only word she has left, and then she is crossing the floor.
He kneels to meet her. His great stone arms close around her, careful, the way a man holds something he almost lost for good. Her forehead rests against the warm brass of his chest.
Beside you the lantern burns bright and steady. Far below, a boy has kept a lamp for his father all this time. Soon he will not have to keep it alone.
